# Full catalogue upgrade fixture

The dedicated `f200/cross-to-f210` 4.7.20003 source and `f210/cross-from-f200` successor form the F200 Base 2.0.77 saved-state hop to F210 Base 2.1.23. The successor preflights the retained six-pack science-productivity identity before the existing gear-only lab accelerator writes, preserves the protected input save and exercises the ordinary successor save plus two cold reloads. Its host controls model the required raw/state boundary only; native research, save, migration and performance qualification remain separate.

For both dedicated cross-engine stages, compose the four selected stage files with `shared/control.lua` as `fixture_control.lua`, `shared/data-final-fixes.lua` as `fixture_data_final.lua`, and `shared/f210-catalogue.lua` as `f210_catalogue.lua`. The F200 cross source needs that last alias too. Use `full-catalogue-cross-f200-f210-published-f200-2077.json` for source fixture0.2.1 and `full-catalogue-cross-f200-f210-mir5-f210-2123.json` for successor0.3.0. Run the existing native fixture command on the exact2.0.77 source first; pass its original completed ZIP and SHA256 to the separate2.1.23 successor with `-InputSavePath` and `-ExpectedInputSaveSha256`. Keep all source/target archives, engine identities and controls distinct; neither profile is a native pass.

This private two-stage fixture uses the frozen `modern-f200-470.json` and `modern-f210-470.json` inventories to exercise one exact published 4.7.2 to MIR5 saved-game transition for each target's Base and all-official Space Age closure. It explicitly level-seeds every recovered non-scripted public technology and each retained Space Age native owner. The two scripted carrier IDs are checked for presence but deliberately not seeded; their runtime behavior belongs to separate scripted-effect qualifications.

The only actual research work is one gear level before and one after the configuration transition. The saved source state retains a 42% current gear queue and a separate force's detached 27% gear progress. The paused force's complete declared technology, recipe, native-force, and gun-effect snapshot is also retained across the upgrade and cold reloads. Recipe bonuses and explicit native force effect fields are snapshotted before and after the upgrade. The named hidden zero-credit carriers are allowed only when their exact private identities are disabled and effect-free.

Both target stage folders contain only their exact `info.json`, target catalogue wrapper, and thin common-module loaders. The native stager must package the selected target stage files together with `shared/control.lua` as `fixture_control.lua`, `shared/data-final-fixes.lua` as `fixture_data_final.lua`, and, for F210 only, `shared/f210-catalogue.lua` as `f210_catalogue.lua`. This is explicit finite fixture composition, not player-source import or fixture discovery.

The F210 source profiles bind published `more-infinite-research_4.7.21002.zip` SHA256 `A4BB8F47232C689B267EF434F557187A8795C47280FA464169DE917FB579517F`; the successor profiles bind the frozen dispatch candidate SHA256 `C8E0C570213F41CA8C816A29D1556FD40A36896D31ED56B07856652B2DE7F32A`. The five F210 Space Age native owners are finite published-source records selected from the independent `modern-f210-470.json` captured bindings and are read/snapshotted on the published stage before successor preservation is checked.

The separate F210 `published-4.7.3` and `mir5-from-4.7.3` stages preserve the same finite catalogue/control composition while binding exact published `more-infinite-research_4.7.21003.zip` SHA256 `B6EB9430056ABD384DB00F94929FE7DAC0A37441ACF4BC277946689682628852` and current `more-infinite-research_5.0.21000.zip` SHA256 `8F858F6B7E604757DE84D960E7D7701021B956782C65A13978E3AFD711F7B071`. Their wrappers alter only the returned fixture target's `published_mir` to `4.7.21003`; the old4.7.21002 source stages, their profiles, and their evidence retain their original identities. The profiles are selection inputs, not native verdicts. The separate [B6-to8F composite](../../../spec/evidence/full-catalogue-473-8f-native-chain.json) now records four actual Base/Space Age stages, four real gear completions and eight read-only cold reloads, preserving its original caller-count adverse and reusing the completed Space Age source save for only the missing successor. Those results retain their actual controller/profile/fixture/archive identities; they do not qualify an arbitrary later rebind. The finite53 Base/71 Space Age row plan still comes from modern-f210-470.json. Before claiming complete B6 catalogue coverage, independently establish the default B6 row-set or its equivalence to that plan; correct B6 archive binding alone does not exclude an unseeded published row.

Native execution is required. The focused Python controls prove static independent-inventory closure, data-stage guard behavior, profile closure, and callback boundaries; they do not simulate Factorio research, source-stage owner state, configuration migration, save hand-off, or either cold reload.

Before accelerating either arm's gear witness, the shared data-stage guard checks the four ordered science ingredients and their unit quantities against the independent F200/F210 captured workload. Missing, changed or duplicated science inputs refuse before any workload mutation; provisioning labs from the candidate's own ingredients alone would conceal those differences.
